Polyaspartic Coatings

What Is Polyaspartic & Why Choose It?

Polyaspartic is a next-generation floor coating chemistry that's related to polyurea. It was developed to address specific limitations of traditional epoxy: UV yellowing in direct sunlight, long cure times, and susceptibility to hot tire transfer. If you've ever seen an older epoxy floor in a home garage that's turned yellow near the windows or doors, you've seen what UV exposure does to standard epoxy.

Polyaspartic coatings are 100% UV-stable — they won't yellow or chalk even in south-facing garages that get direct afternoon sun through open doors. They're also significantly harder than epoxy, with higher abrasion resistance and better resistance to hot tire pickup (the blistering that can happen when you park a hot car on an epoxy floor in summer).

The fast cure rate is a major practical advantage. Traditional epoxy systems require 24–72 hours of cure time before foot traffic and up to a week before vehicle traffic. A polyaspartic system installed in the morning can handle foot traffic by afternoon and vehicle traffic within 24 hours — ideal for households that use the garage daily or businesses that can't afford extended downtime.
